identity.title: Discovery of 22 GHz Water Masers in the Serpens South Region

paper_type_evidence.quote: Using the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA), we have conducted a survey for 22 GHz, $6_{1,6}$–$5_{2,3}$ H$_2$O masers toward the Serpens South region.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA #2012.1.00769.S and #2015.1.00283.S.

question.value: Do low-mass protostars in Serpens South host 22 GHz H2O masers, where do the masers arise, and how does maser emission relate to bolometric luminosity?

evidence.quote: We detect for the first time H$_2$O masers in the Serpens South region that are found to be associated to three Class 0–Class I objects
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA #2012.1.00769.S and #2015.1.00283.S.

evidence.quote: the dust disk detected in the ALMA continuum map at 347 GHz shown in Fig. [13](#fig:alma-cont-347) of Appendix [6](#sec:appendix).
We observed the $6_{1,6} - 5_{2,3}$ H$_2$O maser line (at rest frequency 22,235.080 MHz)

provided.value: 22 GHz H2O maser survey of 48 fields plus 22.9 GHz continuum (program 18B-230)

evidence.quote: under program 18B-230
These observations were conducted between March and November, 2020 as part of program BO061

what.value: ALMA CO(2-1) outflow of CARMA-7/CARMA-6 used for comparison with maser positions

evidence.loc: Results, VLA detected sources with H$_2$O emission
evidence.quote: The water maser detected with the VLA toward CARMA-7 is found at the very base of the CO ($J$=2–1) molecular outflow (see Fig. [3](#fig:outflows)) traced by ALMA (cite: Plunkett_2015).
Extinction corrected bolometric luminosities are available for the 162 stars of the catalog by (cite: Dunham_2015)

results_numeric.quantity: Bolometric luminosity threshold for water masers

evidence.quote: Figure [9](#fig:lbol) suggests that there is a bolometric luminosity threshold of $L_{\rm Bol}\approx10~L_\odot$ to excite water maser emission.

results_numeric.quantity: New radio continuum detections at 22 GHz

evidence.quote: Therefore, we are reporting 6+5=11 new radio continuum detections.

results_numeric.quantity: Offset of CARMA-6 masers from ALMA 347 GHz continuum peak

evidence.quote: have a significatn offset of 50 mas ($\approx22$ au) with respect to the continuum peak

findings_qualitative.value: Masers in the three Class 0–I sources lie at the base of outflows and are likely shock-excited; SSTgbs J1830177–021211 is likely a background AGB star.

evidence.quote: suggest that SSTgbs J1830177–021211 is most likely a background AGB star

claims.hypothesis: Water masers exist in Serpens South protostars
claims.experiment: VLA 22 GHz survey of 48 fields, VLBA follow-up
claims.result: Masers in CARMA-7, CARMA-6, SSTgbs J1829053–014156, SSTgbs J1830177–021211
claims.finding: First detection of H2O masers in the region

evidence.quote: The VLA observations revealed, for the first time, three water masers in the region

claims.hypothesis: A luminosity threshold exists for maser hosting
claims.experiment: Compare L_Bol distributions of hosts and 162 YSOs
claims.finding: Suggested threshold, but variability may hide lower-luminosity masers

evidence.quote: However, the water masers show strong variability, thus lower-luminosity sources may have been missed by the observations.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Rotating protostellar jet for CARMA-6 velocity gradient disfavoured since jet perpendicular to ALMA disk (PA 172°) differs from maser filament (≈130°).

evidence.quote: This seems to work against a rotating protostellar jet as the explanation for the observed maser velocity gradient.

limitations_admitted.value: VLBA time baseline too short for kinematics; parallax not constrained.

evidence.quote: covering a time baseline too short to investigate the internal kinematics of the masers.

referee_caveats_inferred: ALMA is used only for comparison images; no ALMA processing described
Luminosity threshold based on only 4 maser hosts and variable masers

missing_for_reproduction: ALMA data processing details for the 347 GHz map
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ALMA part small (~tens of GB); VLA/VLBA data separate
reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA is a minor comparison and no ALMA reduction is described.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Main results come from VLA/VLBA, not ALMA.
